info.title: HYDRA-UMC-SERVER API
info.description: OpenAPI description of the part of HYDRA-UMC-SERVER's HTTP surface that a typed client needs to discover a server, sign in, read and write its fleet roster and dispatch a robot command. It is a subset: the server's own docs/openapi.json is generated from the server and lists every route (administration, cameras, CAN OTA, system services and more), so use that one when a route is not here. Response objects may gain fields: a client must ignore the ones it does not know. Every route except GET /api/hydra-info, POST /api/login, POST /api/refresh and POST /api/logout needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. One disclosed difference with docs/API_DESIGN.md: that design describes command results as ACCEPTED/REJECTED/RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED with a correlation identifier, while POST /api/robot/{id}/command replies with a plain {success, affectedCount} once the change has been applied and broadcast. Contract v2, block 1 (claims by controller, jog arming and the server-side safety limits) is described by the routes tagged `claims` and `safety`; a client that sends no `controllerId` gets the v1 behaviour. Contract v2, blocks 2 to 5: `GET /api/robot/{id}` answers one robot with its revision (the `ETag`), `If-Match` on `command`, `claim` and `release` is answered with `412` when the robot changed, the `table` command moves the XY table in one request, `GET /api/audit` (administrators) reads the audit record, and the WebSocket message `claims` (clients that opened `/ws` with `?remoteApiVersion=2`) pushes the list of `GET /api/claims`.

servers.description: HYDRA-UMC-SERVER's own default bind address (see HYDRA-UMC-SERVER/src/server.ts's defaultServerURL-equivalent and HYDRA-UMC-TOOL-CLI's own defaultServerURL, which both point here).

tags.name: discovery
tags.description: Unauthenticated server identity/health, per docs/CONTRACTS.md's ServerDiscovery contract.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: JWT issuance for every other authenticated route below.

tags.name: fleet
tags.description: The real controller/robot roster - the read plane docs/API_DESIGN.md describes.

tags.name: command
tags.description: Real-time, per-robot atomic commands - the command plane docs/API_DESIGN.md describes.

tags.name: claims
tags.description: Exclusive, time-limited control of a robot by an account and, optionally, by one controller of that account.

tags.name: safety
tags.description: Limits kept in the server (jog size, bed temperature) and the explicit arming of the jog.

tags.name: ecosystem
tags.description: The read-only health of the services of the ecosystem.

get.summary: Real server identity and discovery metadata
get.description: Unauthenticated by default. Real, per-client remote-access gating (Config > Remote Access) can make this respond 404 for a given X-Hydra-Client caller instead of exposing whether a server exists at all at that address.

parameters.name: X-Hydra-Client
parameters.description: Identifies which real client is asking (e.g. suite, android, ios), so the per-client remote-access gate in Config can allow/deny it independently of the others.

200.description: Real server identity, mirroring the published ServerDiscovery contract (contracts/json-schema/v1/server-discovery.schema.json).

404.description: Remote access is disabled for this X-Hydra-Client caller - deliberately indistinguishable from 'no server running here' to a scanning client. Empty body.

post.summary: Authenticate with a local username/password and obtain a JWT

200.description: Real JWT issued - pass it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every route below tagged with bearerAuth.

401.description: Real invalid-credentials rejection - same message for an unknown username and a wrong password, on purpose (never confirms which one was wrong). When the account has the second step on and no valid `totp` was sent, the body also carries `totpRequired: true`.

429.description: Too many failed sign-in attempts from this address; wait for the window to pass.

get.summary: Read the real, current full settings document, including the controller/robot roster
get.description: Any signed-in account may read it (an administrator also sees the camera credentials). The `settings` object is intentionally not modeled field by field: the server treats it as an opaque, forward-compatible blob - only the `controllers` roster that typed clients consume is modeled below. The response carries an `ETag`; send it back as `If-Match` when saving.

500.description: The settings file on disk could not be read.

post.summary: Replace the real settings document (admin only)
post.description: Real, admin-only write. Persists the payload verbatim (queued, debounced disk write) and broadcasts it to every other connected client - and, on a real HYDRA-UMC-SERVER build with the camera process supervisor, reconciles each camera's own capture process against its new configuration.

409.description: The document changed since the revision in If-Match.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag received with the document being replaced. When it no longer matches, the write is refused with 409 instead of overwriting another client's change.

post.summary: Dispatch one real, atomic, broadcast command to a robot (and its combined sibling, where the command type fans out)
post.description: Real command plane: mutates in-memory state, queues a debounced full-settings write, and broadcasts a small per-robot delta to every other connected client via the same request/response cycle - there is no separate polling step. See this document's own top-level description for the real (not the aspirational ACCEPTED/REJECTED/... ) response shape. A command that is recognised but whose parameters were discarded still answers 200 and lists the discarded field in `warnings`. The optional controller id (`X-Controller-Id` header or `controllerId` in the body) names the client that sends it; while `jog.armRequired` is on a `jog` needs the robot to be armed first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A real robot's own numeric id (distinct from a controller's own, sometimes string, id - see HYDRA-UMC-TOOL-CLI's own robots.go for that real, confirmed API inconsistency).

200.description: Real, applied mutation - see this document's own top-level description for why this is not the ACCEPTED/REJECTED/... envelope docs/API_DESIGN.md describes.

400.description: The command is unknown, or its parameters are invalid (a trajectory outside 1-10000 points, for example). A refused `table` move is `400` with `table-invalid`, `table-out-of-limit` or `table-missing`, and nothing changed.

404.description: No robot with this id exists in the current settings document.

409.description: A robot this command would move is claimed by another account (`other-account`), by another controller of your account (`other-controller`) or by a controller you did not name (`controller-id-required`). `stop` is never blocked.

403.description: The jog is not armed for this robot (`jog-not-armed`); arm it with `POST /api/robot/{id}/jog-arm`. Or `enable` is refused: `enable-not-allowed` (the server option is off, the default) or `admin-required`.

412.description: `If-Match` did not agree with the robot (`revision-mismatch`): read it again with `GET /api/robot/{id}` and retry.

423.description: The robot is disabled (`robot-disabled`): only `stop`, `disable` and `enable` work on it until it is enabled again.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new access token
post.description: No bearer token needed: the refresh token is the credential. It is single use; the response carries its replacement.

200.description: A new access token and a new refresh token.

401.description: The refresh token is unknown, expired or revoked.

429.description: Too many refresh attempts from this address.

post.description: Always answers success: an unknown or already used token is not an error.

post.summary: Take exclusive, time-limited control of a robot
post.description: Re-claiming your own claim renews it. With a controller id the claim belongs to that controller of the account.

400.description: `invalid-controller-id`, or `controller-id-required` when the server demands one to claim.

409.description: Claimed by another account (`other-account`) or by another controller of your account (`other-controller`).

412.description: `If-Match` did not agree with the robot (`revision-mismatch`): read it again with `GET /api/robot/{id}` and retry.

post.summary: Give up the claim on a robot
post.description: Idempotent: releasing a robot nobody claims succeeds. Only the holder (same account and, when the claim has one, same controller) or an administrator may release.

200.description: The robot is not claimed any more.

409.description: Held by another account, by another controller or by a controller that must be named (`other-account`, `other-controller`, `controller-id-required`).

412.description: `If-Match` did not agree with the robot (`revision-mismatch`): read it again with `GET /api/robot/{id}` and retry.

post.summary: Arm or disarm the jog of a robot
post.description: The arming belongs to the account and controller that made it, lasts at most `jog.armTtlMs` and is only demanded while `jog.armRequired` is on. `stop`, the global stop and `release` clear it.

409.description: Another account or controller holds the claim.

get.summary: The safety limits every client is held to

parameters.name: robotId
parameters.description: Adds the limits of that robot model and its jog arming.

200.description: Saved; the answer carries the limits now in force.

400.description: An unknown key, a wrong type or a value beyond the hard ceilings.

get.description: Send the revision back as `If-Match` on `command`, `claim` or `release` to be refused when the robot changed in between.

200.description: The robot, its revision and the header `ETag`.

get.description: The newest entries, oldest first. `format=jsonl` downloads the lines as stored.

get.summary: The health of the services of the ecosystem (operators and administrators)
get.description: Read only. It answers only once an administrator turned on `ecosystemHealth.enabled`; while it is off a signed-in client gets a plain `404` with no body, exactly as a server without the route would answer. A viewer gets `403`. The port, health path, unit and active state of each service are only in the answer to an administrator.

503.description: The health could not be read.

get.summary: The signal of life of each robot of the roster
get.description: `live` when the server had news of the robot (a command it carried out, a change of its state or a heartbeat) within `stale_after_s`, `stale` when the last news is older and `unknown` when there has been none since the server started. It is not the `online` flag of the settings and not a measurement of the hardware.

post.summary: Tell the server that a robot is alive (administrators and operators)
post.description: For a bridge or controller account that has real news of a robot. No body.

404.description: No robot with this id in the roster.

post.summary: Say that the global stop is over (administrators)
post.description: Publishes the retained `READY` on the MQTT bridge when announcing the global stop is configured (`announced: false` otherwise or when the broker is not connected). It moves no robot and is written to the audit record. No body.

403.description: The account is not an administrator.

code.description: Stable refusal codes: `other-account`, `other-controller`, `controller-id-required`, `invalid-controller-id`, `jog-not-armed`, `revision-mismatch`, `table-invalid`, `table-out-of-limit`, `table-missing`. A client must keep an unknown code as a plain error.

totpRequired.description: Present on a sign-in answered with 401 or 429 when the account has the second step on: the sign-in must be repeated with `totp`.

ServerDiscovery.description: Mirrors contracts/json-schema/v1/server-discovery.schema.json field-for-field - restated here natively rather than $ref'd across schema drafts, since that file's own $id/$schema target JSON Schema 2020-12 directly rather than through OpenAPI's Schema Object.

totp.description: The code of the second step (a 6-digit code from an authenticator app or an unused recovery code). Only for an account that turned the second step on; sending it for one that did not is harmless.

token.description: A signed JWT (see JWT_EXPIRES_IN for this server's configured lifetime, default 30d).

role.description: e.g. "admin" or "operator" - see docs/CONTRACTS.md's account-management notes.

refreshToken.description: An opaque, single-use refresh token (90 days by default). Exchange it at POST /api/refresh for a new access token and a new refresh token.

RobotRosterEntry.description: Only the roster-level fields real typed clients (e.g. HYDRA-UMC-TOOL-CLI's own robots.go) actually consume are modeled - a real robot object carries many more live-state fields (pos, joints, playbackState, valves, pumps, camera, xyTable, ...) not exhaustively typed here, matching this contract's own additive philosophy.

id.description: A real robot's own numeric id - distinct from a controller's own id, which may be a string.

combinedWith.description: Sibling robot ids that share this robot's non-trajectory commands (see the command plane's own affectedIds rule).

id.description: A real controller's own id - may be a string (e.g. "localhost" for the default local controller) even though a robot's own id is always numeric; a real, confirmed API inconsistency, not a typo.

SettingsDocument.description: The real, full settings document persisted to data/settings.json. `settings` is deliberately left opaque (type: object only) - it carries UI layout, integrations, gamepad mapping, and other fields the server itself treats as an untyped blob it never validates; only `controllers` is modeled to roster depth, since that is the real, stable surface existing typed clients already depend on.

affectedCount.description: How many robots this one command actually touched - more than 1 only for a non-trajectory command on a combined pair (see combinedWith).

warnings.description: Present when part of a recognised command was discarded (for example a speed outside 10-500, a jog with an unknown axis, a valve index outside 0-7).

revision.description: The new revision of the robot the command was sent to (also the `ETag`).

applied.description: Only after a `table` move: the position the table ended in.

CommandStop.description: Stops playback now (also stops this robot's own server-side playback timer) and clears isPlaying/activeStep/isPaused/isFinished.

CommandPlay.description: Starts playback from step 0 (also starts this robot's own server-side playback timer).

CommandPause.description: Toggles pause by default; `params.paused` sets an explicit desired state instead, so a combined pair can never end up with one paused member and one not.

CommandJog.description: Relative (or, with absolute:true, absolute) single-axis motion. target:"xytable" only honors axis x/y and requires the robot to have a configured XY table; target:"robot" (default) applies to any of x/y/z/a/b/c and accepts an optional client-computed joints override (validated as 6 finite numbers, else the server falls back to its own generic IK).

absolute.description: Set the axis to amount instead of adding amount to it.

joints.description: Optional client-computed joint override, only honored for target:"robot".

CommandReset.description: target:"robot" (default) zeroes pos/joints to home (tx/ty/trz preserved); target:"xytable" zeroes only the XY table's own pos and pos.tx/ty, leaving the arm's own pose untouched.

joints.description: Optional client-supplied home pose (e.g. a per-model homePoseFor(robot.model)); falls back to the server's own generic IK if omitted/invalid.

CommandJogStep.description: Sets this robot's own server-synced jog step size, used by subsequent "jog" commands' own client-side amount calculation.

CommandReset3D.description: Signals every OTHER connected client to remount its own local 3D camera view for this robot - no real robot motion or state change.

CommandTool.description: Sets the robot's currently mounted end-effector/tool label.

CommandValve.description: Sets one pneumatic valve's open/closed state.

CommandPump.description: Sets one vacuum pump's on/off state.

CommandSpeed.description: Sets playback speed and/or acceleration, each independently optional; at least one is expected to be present for this command to have any effect.

CommandTrajectory.description: Loads and selects a full point list as this robot's own Work, validated and prepared BEFORE any state is touched (so a racing Play command can never replay a stale trajectory). Unlike every other command, this never applies to a combined sibling - a trajectory belongs to exactly one robot.

TrajectoryPoint.description: Every field is optional per point, but the point must carry either all 6 native joints (j1..j6) or a full Cartesian pose (x, y, z) - checked after this shape validates. tx/ty/trz (XY table axes) are only accepted on a robot with a configured XY table.

CommandVision.description: Enables/disables this robot's own vision pipeline, and its assigned camera's connected flag alongside it.

retryAfterMs.description: The length of the rate-limit window.

revision.description: The revision of the document just written (the value of the next ETag).
The revision the server holds now.

code.description: `other-account`, `other-controller` or `controller-id-required`; absent on a server that predates the codes.

ControllerId.description: Chosen by one control client for its session.

force.description: An administrator may take over an active claim.

revision.description: The new revision of the robot (also the `ETag`).

controllerId.description: The controller that holds the claim, null for a claim made without one. This is not the cell id of the settings tree.

jogArmedUntil.description: When the arming of the jog of this robot ends, null when it is not armed.

limits.description: The limits in force: `jog` (armRequired, armTtlMs, default, models), `temperature` (default, models) and `claims` (requireControllerId).

hardLimits.description: Ceilings that no setting can pass.

robot.description: Present with `robotId`: the limits that apply to that robot model and, when its jog is armed, `jogArmedUntil`.

SafetyLimitsPatch.description: A partial change, validated by the server. An object under `models` replaces the whole table of that section; models are keyed by name without the parenthesis and without case.

revision.description: The current revision of the robot.

robot.description: The robot as the server holds it; the credentials of the cameras are left out unless the caller is an administrator.

revision.description: Fingerprint of the robot, also the `ETag` of the answer. The record of past claims, the times of a claim and the step counter of a running playback are not part of it.

cellId.description: The cell (controller of the settings tree) the robot belongs to.

CommandTable.description: One move of the XY table of a robot in one request. It is checked as a whole before anything changes (finite numbers; a relative move within the largest jog of the model, an absolute one and the position a move ends in within the largest absolute position) and needs the claim like every command but `stop`, and the arming while it is demanded. The robot must have a configured XY table. It touches the robot it is sent to, never its combined siblings.

prev.description: SHA-256 of the previous line (64 zeros for the first).

hash.description: SHA-256 of this line without this field.

lockedOff.description: True when the environment of the deployment switched the record off.

verification.description: Only with `verify=1`: whether the hash chain of every file is intact.

ClaimsEvent.description: WebSocket message pushed to the clients that opened `/ws` with `?remoteApiVersion=2` after a claim, a release, an arming or a stop changed. A claim that merely expires is not announced.

CommandDisable.description: Puts one robot in safe mode: it stops, its valves and pumps go off, the arming of its jog is dropped and it is marked `enabled: false`. Every other command of the robot except `stop` and `enable` is then refused with `423` (`robot-disabled`). Like `stop` it is open to every signed-in account and is never blocked by a claim or a stale revision. It touches only the robot it is sent to.

CommandEnable.description: Brings a robot in safe mode back and restarts nothing (it stays stopped; the jog has to be armed again). It is off by default: `403` with `enable-not-allowed` until an administrator turns on `robots.allowEnable` on the server, and then only an administrator may use it (`403` with `admin-required`). The claim check applies as for any command but `stop`. It touches only the robot it is sent to.

EcosystemHealth.title: EcosystemHealth
EcosystemHealth.description: The read-only health of the services of the ecosystem that a server answers at GET /api/ecosystem/health: for each service that declares a port or a unit, whether it answers, the version it reports against the one its manifest expects, and the state of the TLS certificate of the server itself. The port, health path, unit and active state of a service are only in the answer to an administrator.

available.description: False when the sibling checkouts could not be scanned at all (then there are no services).

drift.description: True only when both versions are known and differ.

anyOf.description: The TLS certificate of the server itself; null when it runs without TLS. The path and the key are never part of it.

RobotLiveness.title: RobotLiveness
RobotLiveness.description: The signal of life of each robot of the roster that a server answers at GET /api/robots/liveness: live when the server had news of the robot within stale_after_s, stale when the last news is older and unknown when there has been none since the server started. It is news the server received, not a measurement of the hardware, and it is not the online flag of the settings.

last_update_utc.description: Absent while the state is unknown.

age_s.description: Absent while the state is unknown.

source.description: Absent while the state is unknown.

announced.description: Whether the retained READY went out on the MQTT bridge. False when announcing the global stop is not configured or the broker is not connected.

ControllerIdHeader.name: X-Controller-Id
ControllerIdHeader.description: The identity one control client (a window, a tab, a phone) picked for its session: 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits and `. _ : -`. The same value may be sent as `controllerId` in the JSON body; the header wins when both are present. Omitted, the request behaves as in v1.

IfMatchHeader.name: If-Match
IfMatchHeader.description: The revision of the robot as `GET /api/robot/{id}` (or the last answer) gave it, quoted or not; `*` always agrees. When the robot changed since, the answer is `412` with the current revision. A `stop` is never conditional. Without the header the request is unconditional, as in v1.
